task: E1 — does the physics baseline decelerate? (ADR-064)
question: ELMFIRE is Rothermel, i.e. rate of spread along a perimeter, so it is perimeter-proportional like our kernel. Does it ACCELERATE as a fire ages, the way our kernel does, or DECELERATE, the way real fires do?

pre_registration.source: ADR-064 (4), written before any ELMFIRE output existed
pre_registration.E-P1: ELMFIRE's stage_decay is POSITIVE (accelerating) on >= 4 of the 5 currently held-out blocks
pre_registration.E-P2: its magnitude sits BETWEEN our kernel's and truth's
pre_registration.E-P3: it gets DOLAN (block 6) closer to right than arm S does, because Dolan is remote and least suppressed
pre_registration.decision_rule: >=4/5 positive -> the defect belongs to the model CLASS. >=4/5 negative -> E-P1 REFUTED and the defect is ours. 3/5 either way -> not_a_verdict.

estimator: eval/stage.py UNCHANGED — the same code that judged truth, arm A and arm S. No second implementation exists in this module (ADR-064 (6)).

scoring_code_fingerprint.status: PROPOSAL — reported, not enforced. `git_sha` is real but NOT identifying while `git_dirty` is true for every run; this is.

licence.registry_refusal: 'stage_decay' is not in C6_METRICS, so nothing has ruled on whether it may decide the E1 ELMFIRE stage experiment. An unregistered metric is an unchecked metric; register it with a direction and a gate_eligible flag before letting it decide anything.

headline_member_prefix_note: every block is read at the SAME ensemble size — the minimum available across the fires — so no block's number comes from a bigger ensemble than another's. `member_prefix_sensitivity` shows the same estimator at every other available size.

declared_deviations_from_elmfire_default.direction: FINER than the default, i.e. a more accurate level-set solve, not a faster or more favourable one. It is not a Rothermel parameter.
declared_deviations_from_elmfire_default.cost: 5x the runtime. This is the single reason block 4 (Creek, 785 windows, 78% of the total compute) is expensive: at t0=62 one window already costs ~717 s. It was NOT changed mid-experiment — altering a solver setting after seeing that a run is slow is how one experiment becomes two. A future full-14-block run should decide it BEFORE starting.

declared_deviations_from_elmfire_default.direction: DANGEROUS, and it is why this is declared rather than left implicit. `elmfire_level_set.f90:1263` compares it against WALL-CLOCK elapsed time and, when exceeded, sets `T = TSTOP + 1` and stops the simulation early. Nothing in the rasters says so. A capped run therefore UNDER-reports late-window growth, which biases stage_decay DOWN — toward deceleration, i.e. AGAINST E-P1 — and, because the cap is wall-clock, whether it bites depends on machine load and worker count rather than on the fire.
declared_deviations_from_elmfire_default.cost: MEASURED, not assumed: across the scored blocks the worst window costs 235 s/member against a 600 s cap on the four blocks scored here (2.55x margin, 0 windows within 50% of the cap), so those blocks are cap-independent; Creek reaches 385 s/member by t0=124 and rises, which is why it is the block that did not finish. Any window within `TRUNCATION_FRACTION` of the cap is refused by `score`.

declared_deviations_from_elmfire_default.direction: we take ELMFIRE's own default. Recorded because our kernel HAS a long-range spot component, so the comparison is a spotting model against a non-spotting one. Carried from S4's fairness note.

sign_test_positive_direction.note: One-sided exact binomial tail at p=0.5, i.e. the chance of seeing at least this many blocks pointing one way if each block were a coin flip. It tests DIRECTION and says nothing about magnitude.

verdict_reason: 4 of 4 scored blocks are POSITIVE (accelerating), with 1 block(s) not scored. The count can only RISE, so the final tally is >= 4/5 under every possible completion and ADR-064 (4)'s >=4/5 threshold is met either way. The MAGNITUDE columns are still incomplete; only the sign count is determined.

mapping_compromises.issue: 30 m does not divide 1000 m, so a true-30 m grid is not nested
mapping_compromises.choice: exactly nested refine=33 -> 30.303 m (1.01% off native)
mapping_compromises.bias: none directional. The alternative puts area conservation inside partial-overlap weights, where an area loss can hide.

mapping_compromises.issue: C5 must return uint8 fire_state on the 1 km C1 lattice
mapping_compromises.choice: fractional-area occupancy: block-mean the binary fine mask over the exactly nested R x R sub-cell block, burned iff covered fraction >= 0.5. Identical in form and threshold to data/rasterize.polygon_mask, which defines TRUTH.
mapping_compromises.bias: measured, not asserted: exact on resolvable features; a fire finger narrower than 1 km is UNREPRESENTABLE at 1 km by any binary rule (500 m finger retains 67% of its area in 6 fragments). Biases ELMFIRE LOW on fine fingering, which is the flattering direction and is why it is measured in reports/figures/playthrough_coarsening.json.

mapping_compromises.issue: ELMFIRE would ideally take RTMA on its own grid
mapping_compromises.choice: C1 channels 1-4 + 11 at 1 km, written as a separate coarser weather raster
mapping_compromises.bias: none: RTMA is natively 2.5 km, so the 1 km C1 field is an UPSAMPLING and carries everything RTMA had.

mapping_compromises.issue: elmfire_subs.f90:815 `J2 = MAX(MIN(J2+1, NROW_WX),1)` reads J2, an INTENT(OUT) argument, before it is set — the x-axis line above it correctly uses I1+1. A second uninitialised read, found by simviz.
mapping_compromises.choice: set .FALSE. (nearest weather cell) rather than patch the physics
mapping_compromises.bias: negligible at 1 km weather over a 2.5 km native product. Deliberately NOT patched: my standard for touching a baseline's source is that the change be provably output-neutral, and J1+1 would change results.

mapping_compromises.issue: C1 carries ONE fuel_moisture_proxy; Rothermel wants three dead classes
mapping_compromises.choice: m1 = proxy, m10 = proxy + 1 pt, m100 = proxy + 2 pt
mapping_compromises.bias: unknown, small; the +1/+2 offsets are conventional, not measured here

mapping_compromises.issue: RTMA is 10 m wind in m/s; ELMFIRE wants 20 ft wind in mph
mapping_compromises.choice: log profile z0=0.03 m -> x0.8703, then x2.23694 m/s->mph
mapping_compromises.bias: none intended; the factor is stated so it can be disputed

mapping_compromises.issue: our (u, v) is the vector the wind blows TOWARD; ELMFIRE wd is FROM
mapping_compromises.bias: an error here is a 180 deg flip and would be catastrophic and silent

mapping_compromises.issue: ELMFIRE normally starts from a point ignition
mapping_compromises.choice: our x0 is replicated onto the fine lattice and written into ELMFIRE's level-set field phi (negative inside the burned region)
mapping_compromises.bias: essential. A point-ignition mapping makes ELMFIRE re-grow the fire from scratch inside every window and look absurdly weak for a reason that is ours. Replication is exact — it invents no sub-cell detail.

mapping_compromises.issue: LFPS publishes exactly one topographic vintage, LF2020
mapping_compromises.choice: LF2020 Elev/SlpD/Asp for every fire year
mapping_compromises.bias: none. Terrain is time-invariant at these scales; it is not a leak.

mapping_compromises.issue: ELMFIRE is deterministic; its &MONTE_CARLO randomises ignition LOCATION
mapping_compromises.choice: M replicates with ws/wd/moisture perturbed from a declared PDF
mapping_compromises.bias: OUR construction. Any dispersion number is about the PDF we chose.

mapping_compromises.issue: C1 channels 12 and 13 have no ELMFIRE equivalent
mapping_compromises.choice: not pushed into fuels; native FBFM40 passes through unchanged
mapping_compromises.bias: deliberate — ADR-022 (5) bars a hard non-burnable mask anywhere
